findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in Scope/Testing that the v4 change must REVISE OR REMOVE the existing code-v3 assertions in `test_impact_code.py` — at minimum `test_new_binary_scales_with_churn` (moderate-lane churn scaling, deleted by v4), `test_old_sidecars_byte_unchanged`'s `dead_code == 0.12`, and the moderate `reachable_path == 0.24` case — not merely add new cases.
evidence: `test_new_binary_scales_with_churn` (test_impact_code.py:320-325) asserts a MODERATE maint binary's score scales with churn90 (cold 0.24 vs hot 0.48); v4 states 'Churn stays out of the consequence lanes' — this test's premise is deleted by v4 and will FAIL.

`test_old_sidecars_byte_unchanged` (line 310) asserts `impact_code({"dead_code": True}) == 0.12` (= 0.3 tier × 0.5 churn × 0.8 amp under code-v3); v4's debt-lane amplifier-only churn (min 1.0) makes cold dead_code = 0.3 × 1.0 × 0.8 = 0.24, breaking this literal.

Line 289 asserts `reachable_path_without_automated_coverage == 0.24` (moderate, churn-multiplied); v4 re-scopes the moderate lane to `× prod_impact mult × 0.75 rare`, dropping churn — the value changes.

The plan's Testing bullet and AC line 1 enumerate only NEW v4 cases (serious undamped, prod_impact keying, churn=0⇒1.0, floor); no line states the pre-existing code-v3 assertions must be updated/removed.
findings.finding: test_impact_code.py is enumerated in Scope, but the plan does not acknowledge that EXISTING code-v3 arithmetic assertions in it regress under the v4 lane split and must be revised or removed — not merely augmented with new cases.
findings.location: Scope (`tests/unit/test_impact_code.py` → v4 lane expectations); Testing; AC line 1
scenarios: Landing v4 arithmetic without editing these three existing tests → CI red on test_impact_code.py despite the plan claiming the file is covered.
An implementer reads 'v4 lane expectations' as additive and leaves `test_new_binary_scales_with_churn` in place, contradicting the v4 debt-amplifier rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Testing/AC line: 'Rewrite the affected code-v3 arithmetic cases in test_impact_code.py: remove/replace test_new_binary_scales_with_churn (moderate lane no longer churn-scaled), update test_old_sidecars_byte_unchanged (dead_code cold now 0.24 under amplifier-only churn), and update the moderate reachable_path expected value to the prod_impact-keyed formula.'

findings.checklist_item: Correct the plan's framing that re-scoping prod_impact 'documents existing behavior': state explicitly that v3's impact_code did NOT consume prod_impact for the maint lane, and show the replay tables account for the resulting maint-lane rescoring (esp. demotion risk for prod=none/low + hot-churn findings) so the 'zero demotions' claim still holds.
evidence: decide.py impact_code() reads _CODE_PROD_BINARIES, _CODE_MAINT_BINARIES, trigger_likelihood, churn90, silent_failure/escapes_automation, hard_to_reverse_surface — prod_impact is NOT referenced anywhere in impact_code
impact_code only reads prod_impact via the mean impact() model, which code-review does not dispatch
Plan: 'The corpus crosstab shows verifiers already answer both this way; the amendment documents existing behavior.' and step-3 'moderate consequence ... × prod_impact mult'
findings.finding: The plan claims re-scoping prod_impact to key the maintainability lane 'documents existing behavior' and yields an 'identical replay', but v3's impact_code never reads prod_impact at all — it reads only the consequence binaries, trigger_likelihood (prod lane), churn90 (maint lane), and the silent flags. So making the v4 maint lane multiply by a prod_impact mult is a genuine change in what the score consumes, not a documentation of behavior; whatever value verifiers historically recorded in prod_impact was inert for the maint lane under v3.
findings.location: Approach step 2(b) and step 3 (moderate consequence lane); 'the amendment documents existing behavior' / 'Replay identical'
scenarios: Offline replay run against real code-v3 sidecars whose maint-lane findings recorded prod_impact=high but scored via churn only — v4 will re-score them via prod_impact, changing priorities the plan asserts are unchanged
A maint finding that recorded prod_impact=none/low but hot churn: v3 scored it up via churn; v4 damps it via prod_impact — a possible demotion the 'zero demotions' claim must account for

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an end-to-end acceptance criterion: a review run over the 8eadb4fbc5 fire-case diff produces a BLOCKING tests verdict (finding raised, forbids_contract_allowed_state=TRUE, priority>=0.54 under tests@0.54), exercising the composed Pass-1/2/3+routing path rather than each layer in isolation.
evidence: Title: 'Code review cannot block consequential test findings' — the deliverable IS the ability to block

'Replay: the committed replay script re-run against the landed formula reproduces the recorded v4 would-block set' — the plan calls replay offline analysis, not a live gate run: 'the replay is offline analysis, not a migration'
Evals assert the LLM emits the finding/binary; unit tests assert arithmetic; neither asserts the composed gate returns a blocking verdict on the fire case
findings.finding: The plan's headline promise is that the gate CAN NOW BLOCK a consequential test finding, but every test validates a layer in isolation (Pass-1 antipattern emission via eval, Pass-2 binary emission via verify-eval, Pass-3 arithmetic via unit test, routing threshold via pin) and the replay is explicitly offline analysis, not a live run. No acceptance criterion wires the full assembled pipeline on the 8eadb4fbc5 fire-case diff to confirm it produces a BLOCKING verdict end-to-end (finding raised -> binary set -> impact scored -> priority>=0.54 -> tests@0.54 routing blocks). The gate could pass all per-layer tests yet fail to block in production if the layers compose differently than assumed.
findings.location: Testing section + Acceptance Criteria (fire/pass eval + replay bullets)
scenarios: A composition bug (e.g. the fire finding's validity lands in the val<0.5 drop band, or priority=validity×impact for the serious binary lands just under 0.54) leaves the gate green on the fire case while every isolated test passes — the exact regression the ticket exists to prevent ships undetected.

findings.suggested_fix: Specify the full maint-lane mapping, e.g. 'trigger_likelihood: common→×1.0, sometimes→×0.75, rare→×0.75' (or an explicit common=sometimes=1.0, rare=0.75), and ensure the re-scoped trigger_likelihood description in code-review-verify.md / verify_models.py names the maint-lane behavior for each value so it does not conflict with the stated prod-lane 0.6-at-sometimes.

findings.finding: Approach step 2(b) overloads two production-scoped verifier fields (prod_impact, trigger_likelihood) to ALSO mean maint-lane user-reach — a single field now answers two structurally different questions (production harm vs. contract/coverage user-reach), and the maint-lane trigger mapping (×0.75 only when 'rare') differs from the prod-lane ladder (common/sometimes/rare = 1.0/0.6/0.25) on the SAME field. A structurally cleaner alternative is a dedicated maint-lane user-reach attribute (e.g. guarded_path_reach) so the two lanes never share a field with divergent semantics and mappings.
findings.location: Approach step 2(b) 'Re-scope the prod_impact / trigger_likelihood field descriptions'; step 3 'trigger_likelihood=rare ⇒ ×0.75'
